summary: The plausibility-pleading case. A Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal in the S.D.N.Y. is appealed as a final decision to the Second Circuit, which vacates; the defendants win certiorari. Exercises FRCP -> FRAP composition through links.json and the FRCP 12(h) waiver flag carried across forums.

legs.context: Consumers sue the regional Bell companies under Sherman Act § 1 in the S.D.N.Y.; the defendants' Rule 12 response window is open.

steps.event: Defendants move to dismiss the amended complaint under Rule 12(b)(6) instead of answering
Judge Lynch grants the motion: parallel conduct without a plus factor states no § 1 claim
Plaintiffs treat the dismissal as a final decision (28 U.S.C. § 1291) and weigh an appeal
Plaintiffs notice an appeal to the Second Circuit (No. 03-9213)
The appeal crosses into the court of appeals (regional circuit, not the Federal Circuit)
No cross-appeal (the defendants won everything below)
Appeal proceeds; the record is assembled
Appeal from a ruling on the papers: no transcript to order (route assumed; FRAP 10(b)(1)(B))
Nothing to stay: the judgment below only dismissed the complaint (route assumed)
Plaintiffs reply (route assumed; the reply is not in the sources read)
Argued before Sack, Raggi and Hall, JJ.
A Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal is reviewed de novo
Second Circuit vacates the dismissal and remands: parallel conduct can suffice at the pleading stage
Defendants, now the losing party, weigh rehearing
Mandate clock resumes (mandate date not in the sources read)
Bell Atlantic et al. petition for certiorari (No. 05-1126)

gaps.event: Supreme Court reverses and remands (argued 2006-11-27, decided 2007-05-21): a complaint must plead enough facts to make an agreement plausible
gaps.why: No pack models Supreme Court merits review; cert-granted is terminal. A small SCOTUS pack (briefing, argument, affirm/reverse/vacate, remand back to the circuit) would close this for every case here.

deadlines.trigger_event: the S.D.N.Y. dismissal (opinion date; the separate judgment's entry date was not found)
deadlines.arithmetic: FRAP 4(a)(1)(A): 30 days. Oct 8 + 23 = Oct 31; + 7 = Nov 7, a Friday, not a holiday, so no roll.
deadlines.historical: The notice-of-appeal date was not found; the appeal was docketed as No. 03-9213, i.e. in 2003.

deadlines.arithmetic: FRAP 40: 14 days. Oct 3 + 14 = Oct 17, a Monday (Columbus Day was Oct 10, inside the period, which does not matter when counting calendar days).
deadlines.historical: A petition was filed and denied on 2006-01-03; its filing date was not found.

deadlines.trigger_event: denial of rehearing (Sup. Ct. R. 13.3 runs the 90 days from that denial)

quirks: The sources don't say whether the dismissal was with or without prejudice; the pack's only final-dismissal node is dismissed-with-prejudice (granted, no leave to amend), which is what made it appealable.

The FRCP 12(h) waiver flag set by filing a pre-answer motion rides along into the FRAP pack. That is correct graph semantics (flags are history), but it means the appellate nodes are the `{waived-12h-defenses}` copies.
The FRAP pack routes every panel-rehearing denial through an en banc poll; the docket only records 'rehearing denied', so whether en banc rehearing was sought is unknown.
The FRAP pack starts the certiorari window at the mandate; Sup. Ct. R. 13.3 actually runs it from the judgment or the denial of rehearing. The deadline check above uses the rule's trigger.
